title: Materialized Views with REFRESH CONCURRENTLY
realWorldScenario: An executive analytics dashboard aggregates customer lifetime spend and average order values across 10 million orders. The query takes 14 seconds. Running a normal `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW` locks out all dashboard reads for 45 seconds.
questionStatement: Explain how `MATERIALIZED VIEW` works in PostgreSQL. What is the difference between standard `REFRESH` and `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY`? What prerequisite must be met to allow concurrent refresh, and what are the performance trade-offs?
expectedConcepts: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock of standard refresh blocking concurrent reads
REFRESH CONCURRENTLY allowing concurrent SELECT queries
Mandatory UNIQUE index requirement without partial clauses
Diff calculation mechanics using temporary table and unique key
Performance and WAL trade-offs of concurrent refresh
hints: What lock level does standard REFRESH acquire on the table?
Why does Postgres need a unique index to refresh concurrently?
Think about how Postgres compares old rows with new rows.
